idiom_name: struct { enum tag; union { ... } } + switch on the tag
implementation_notes: C has no sum type, so both halves are written by hand: an enumerator for the discriminant and a union for the payloads, wrapped in one struct. The union stores only one member at a time and does not record which one, so the tag is the only thing that makes the value meaningful, and dispatch is a switch over the tag. Anonymous unions with designated initializers (C11) keep construction sites readable. This classic form is the only form available here; as the variant set grows, push construction into functions so callers cannot set the tag and payload inconsistently.
pitfalls: Reading a union member other than the one last stored reinterprets the stored object representation (often with unspecified bytes or a trap representation); the tag does not make an inactive read type-safe, so read only the active member.
Adding a default clause silences -Wswitch, the only exhaustiveness signal C gives you - keep the switch complete and let the warning fire.
A new enumerator compiles silently everywhere; use -Wswitch-enum and grow the variant set in one commit so stale switches are visible.
The struct is as large as the largest payload plus tag and padding; pack hot data separately if memory matters.
